lesson.grammar_point: present simple with I, you and we

listenings.text: Good afternoon, and welcome. My name is Claire Bennett and I teach on this programme. Let me tell you how the first week works, because people always ask. We meet twice a week, on Monday and on Thursday. In every session one student opens the discussion, so everybody speaks at some point in the term. You do not need a long introduction. You say your name, you say what you practise, and you say why you are here. That is enough. Most of the people in this room work full time. We have lawyers, we have two economists, and we have three people who run their own firm. Nobody expects perfect English in this room. We expect you to say what you think, and we expect you to ask when you do not follow.

I meet a lot of lawyers who work in a second language, and they all ask me the same question. How do I introduce myself without sounding small? My answer is short. Do not translate your title. Say what you do. I advise companies that export grain is a better sentence than I am a specialist in agribusiness law, because the first one tells me your work and the second one tells me a label. And then stop talking. The mistake I hear every week is the person who explains twenty years of career before anybody asks for it. Nobody in the room is listening to the history. They are listening for one thing: what does this person actually do on a Tuesday morning? Say that, in one line, and the room understands you.

Brazil sells more sugar and more soya than any other country in the world, and most of that trade never touches a shop. It moves in contracts. A trader in Geneva buys a cargo that is still in the field in Mato Grosso, an insurer in London covers the ship, and a bank in New York pays for it. Every step of that chain is written in English, and every step of it needs a lawyer. That is why so many Brazilian firms now open a small office abroad. They do not open it to find new clients. They open it because the contract, the arbitration and the paperwork all live in another language, and the client wants somebody who reads both.
